sources.title: Buildings Subject to HPD Jurisdiction
sources.publisher: Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD)
sources.coverage_description:
Pursuant to New York City’s Housing Maintenance Code, the Department of Housing 
Preservation and Development (HPD) collects information on multiple dwellings in New York 
City, and other buildings that fall under its jurisdiction. HPD’s Buildings Open Data covers all 
buildings which meet any of the following criteria: 
 
a. HPD has required the owner to register the building under the Housing Maintenance 
Code (HMC) 
b. HPD has initiated a litigation action under the HMC 
c. HPD has received a complaint for the building 
d. HPD has initiated a work order for the purposes of emergency repair, demolition, or 
the Alternative Enforcement Program (AEP) for the building 
e. HPD has added the property to the AEP program

Buildings are identified by a BuildingID.
sources.historical_extent_verification: Publisher coverage description retained. Exact earliest/latest event dates were not independently audited; a completed filtered query is not proof of complete historical agency coverage.

sources.title: Multiple Dwelling Registrations
sources.publisher: Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD)
sources.coverage_description:
Pursuant to New York City’s Housing Maintenance Code, the Department of Housing 
Preservation and Development (HPD) collects registration information from owners of 
residential rental units. Owners are required to register if they own residential buildings 
with three or more units or if they own one- or two-family homes and neither they nor 
members of their immediate family live there. Registrations are required upon taking 
ownership of a qualifying building, and once a year thereafter.

sources.title: Housing Maintenance Code Violations
sources.publisher: Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD)
sources.coverage_description:
Pursuant to New York City’s Housing Maintenance Code, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) issues violations against conditions, in rental dwelling units and buildings, that have been verified to violate the New York City Housing Maintenance Code (HMC) or the New York State Multiple Dwelling Law (MDL).
Each row in this dataset contains discrete information about one violation of the New York City Housing Maintenance Code or New York State Multiple Dwelling Law. Each violation is identified using a unique Violation ID. These Laws are in place to provide requirements for the maintenance of residential dwelling units within New York City. 
Violations are issued by Housing Inspectors after a physical inspection is conducted (except for class I violations which are generally  administratively issued).  Violations are issued in four classes: Class A (non-hazardous), Class B (hazardous), Class C (immediately hazardous) and Class I (information orders).  For more information on violations, see https://www1.nyc.gov/site/hpd/owners/compliance-clear-violations.page  
The base data for this file is all violations open as of October 1, 2012.  Violation data is updated daily.  The daily update includes both new violations and updates to the status of previously issued violations. An open violation is a violation which is still active on the Department records. See the status table for determining how to filter for open violations versus closed violations, and within open violations for a more detailed current status. 
The property owner may or may not have corrected the physical condition if the status is open. The violation status is closed when the violation is observed/verified as corrected by HPD or as certified by the landlord.   The processes for having violations dismissed are described at http://www1.nyc.gov/site/hpd/owners/compliance-clear-violations.page
Using other HPD datasets, such as the Building File or the Registration File, a user can link together violations issued for given buildings or for given owners.

sources.title: DOB Permit Issuance
sources.coverage_description: The Department of Buildings (DOB) issues permits for construction and demolition activities in the City of New York. The construction industry must submit an application to DOB with details of the construction job they would like to complete. The primary types of application, aka job type, are: New Building, Demolition, and Alterations Type 1, 2, and 3. Each job type can have multiple work types, such as general construction, boiler, elevator, and plumbing. Each work type will receive a separate permit. (See the DOB Job Application Filings dataset for information about each job application.) Each row/record in this dataset represents the life cycle of one permit for one work type. The dataset is updated daily with new records, and each existing record will be updated as the permit application moves through the approval process to reflect the latest status of the application. Note: This dataset only includes permits issued in the Buildings Information System (BIS), most current permits are now issued in DOB NOW -- see the DOB NOW: Build – Approved Permits dataset.
sources.historical_extent_verification: Publisher coverage description retained. Exact earliest/latest event dates were not independently audited; a completed filtered query is not proof of complete historical agency coverage.
limitations: Socrata internal :id is used only for stable pagination after agency-ID sorting timed out. Citations still use original permit_si_no; no system ID is represented as an agency ID.

sources.title: OATH Hearings Division Case Status
sources.publisher: Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings (OATH)
sources.coverage_description: NOTE: As of May 4, 2026, the Respondent First Name, Respondent Address (Street Name), Respondent Address (City), and Respondent Address (State Name) fields have been removed from this dataset. All other fields and records remain searchable, or as an alternative, use the OATH Summons Finder or a summons lookup tool from the issuing agency. You can share any questions you have about this change by entering them in the form on nyc.gov/askopendata. The OATH Hearings Division Case Status dataset contains information about alleged public safety and quality of life violations that are filed and adjudicated through the City’s administrative law court, the NYC Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings (OATH) and provides information about the infraction charged, decision outcome, payments, amounts and fees relating to the case. The summonses listed in this dataset are issued and filed at the OATH Hearings Division by City enforcement agencies.
limitations: OATH summons/administrative records are not automatically adjudicated findings. Verify recorded hearing_result separately. FDNY subset only, not all fire inspections.
Exact issuing_agency value FIRE DEPARTMENT OF NYC was observed through the live Zetaris source probe.

sources.title: Buildings Selected for the Alternative Enforcement Program (AEP)
sources.publisher: NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD)
sources.coverage_description: Each year, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) designates severely distressed multiple dwellings for participation in the Alternative Enforcement Program (AEP). HPD is required by law to submit and post an annual summary report of all AEP buildings. This dataset includes all buildings selected for participation in the AEP and the current status of the building in the program.

sources.title: Evictions
sources.coverage_description:
This dataset lists executed evictions within the five boroughs for the years 2017-Present (data prior to January 1, 2017, is not available). The data fields may be sorted by 20 categories of information including Court Index Number, Docket Number, Eviction Address, Marshal First or Last Name, Borough, etc.. 
 
Eviction data is compiled from New York City Marshals. City Marshals are independent public officials appointed by the Mayor. Marshals can be contacted directly regarding evictions, and their contact information can be found at https://www1.nyc.gov/site/doi/offices/marshals-list.page.
limitations: Executed marshal actions are not filings; unit scope is retained. Empty results are not a complete court history.

sources.title: Housing Litigations
sources.publisher: Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD)
sources.coverage_description: The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) Housing Litigation Division (HLD) initiates' actions in the Housing Court against owners of privately-owned buildings to enforce compliance with the housing quality standards contained in the New York State Multiple Dwelling Law and the New York City Housing Maintenance Code.  HLD attorneys also represent HPD when tenants initiate actions against private owners.  HPD is automatically named as party to such actions.  The goal of these court proceedings is to obtain enforceable Orders to Correct, Civil Penalties (fines) and Contempt Sanctions, compelling owners to comply with the Housing Code.
